question: Can I Charge Shipping Based on Order Weight?
metaDescription: Yes — using Flat Rate's cost formula referencing [weight], or a dedicated table rate plugin for more granular weight-based pricing tiers.
shortAnswer: The core Flat Rate shipping method's cost field accepts a formula referencing the cart's total weight (using the [qty], [cost], and similar placeholders alongside per-item weight-based math), letting a basic weight-scaled charge be configured without any additional plugin. For genuinely tiered pricing (a specific rate for 0-5kg, another for 5-10kg, and so on), a dedicated table rate shipping plugin handles this far more cleanly than trying to force it into a single formula.

bodyHtml:
How Weight-Based Charging Works

Flat Rate's cost field supports basic arithmetic and a small set of placeholders representing cart values, which can be combined into a formula approximating weight-based pricing for simpler needs. For real weight-tier pricing with multiple distinct bands and potentially different rates per shipping zone, a table rate plugin provides a proper interface for defining each tier explicitly, rather than maintaining an increasingly complex formula.

Choosing the Right Approach

  • A simple, roughly linear weight-based charge can often be approximated well enough with Flat Rate's formula support, avoiding an extra plugin dependency.
  • Genuine tiered pricing (fixed rates per weight band) is much easier to manage and audit with a dedicated table rate plugin's explicit tier interface.
  • Accurate product weights are essential either way — weight-based shipping is only as accurate as the weight values entered on each product.
  • Combining weight-based rates with shipping classes is possible for products needing both weight scaling and a class-based surcharge, though this adds real configuration complexity worth planning carefully.

Setting This Up

  1. Confirm accurate weight values are entered for every product in the catalog.
  2. Use Flat Rate's formula field for a simple approximation, or install a table rate plugin for genuine tiered pricing.
  3. Test with carts of varying weight to confirm the calculated cost behaves as expected.
